# Fuel Production
Boriatic fuel is the common ship fuel. AME fuel is substantially more expensive and must be produced in two heated stages. Use suitable chemical equipment and keep both fuels away from ignition sources.
## Boriatic Fuel
Heat the mixture to at least [color=orange]300 K[/color]. The recipe below produces three units of fuel from three units of reagents.
## AME Fuel
AME fuel requires an AME catalyst before the final fuel can be mixed.
### Step 1: AME Catalyst
Heat the catalyst mixture to at least [color=orange]370 K[/color].
### Step 2: AME Fuel
Combine the catalyst with boriatic fuel, plasma, and nitrogen, then heat the mixture to at least [color=orange]420 K[/color]. The finished reaction produces two units of AME fuel.
## Asteroid Seeps
Fuel seeps sometimes form inside asteroids. Sand asteroids can hold boriatic fuel, while chromite asteroids can hold raw AME fuel.
Research [color=orange]Seep Extraction[/color], then print an [color=orange]NT-FX-1 seep drill flatpack[/color] at a boriatic composter. Deploy it with a multitool, roll it over a seep, wrench it down and connect it to medium-voltage power.
The drill fills its own tank first, then any refillable container in its cradle. Once both are full, the drill spills excess fuel onto the floor. Seeps never refill.
